title: Suppress benign BecomeMonitor notice in sleep monitor
head: 78775b5da4cf
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Unrelated monitor diagnostics are hidden until the monitor's stderr pipe closes
leads.consequence: grep writes nonmatching lines to a redirected non-TTY stream with ordinary block buffering, rather than passing them through as dbus-monitor prints them. While a producer remains alive, a real warning/error is absent from the journal, so diagnostics sought before the next sleep event or service stop are missing; a clean EOF eventually flushes them. In isolated LC_ALL=C positive/negative controls, the original parent passed 174 bytes while active, the pinned head passed 0 while active and 41 on exit, and adding grep --line-buffered to the pinned head passed 41 while active without restoring the denied notice. The lock request itself still runs, so this is a diagnostics-timing regression rather than proof the inhibitor fails.

leads.summary: Three related open sleep-monitor PRs need an explicit integration decision; one makes this fix redundant
leads.consequence: #10394 changes the same dbus-monitor invocation to gdbus AddMatch to avoid BecomeMonitor, and its added test explicitly rejects 'exec dbus-monitor', so it replaces this PR's premise. #7447 replaces the same command with an absolute DBUS_MONITOR variable; resolving the overlap by retaining only this PR's command drops its Homebrew PATH fix and breaks its added test. #13005 replaces the one coproc producer with two (prepare and resume); retaining its new start_event_monitor without moving the filter means both print the very notice this PR tries to suppress. These heads are diverged, not stacked. Three-way merge-file against each PR's own unchanged base blob 2100ceeb reports a conflict with markers for #10394, #7447, and #13005; GitHub MERGEABLE is relative to current base, not to this head. Other six named overlapping PRs merge without markers and their kept head fixtures pass on the merged monitor.

leads.summary: The claimed sleep-monitor test pass does not exercise any stderr filtering
leads.consequence: Both dbus-monitor stubs only write stdout or sleep; neither emits the BecomeMonitor notice or another stderr error. Mutating the new filter to grep -v . (which drops all nonempty stderr, a plausible overly broad suppression) still passes all four tests with status 0. Adding one stub emitting both lines and an assertion on retained unrelated stderr, preferably before producer exit as well as at exit, would detect this regression. This is a specific test fidelity gap, not a claim that the current lock tests are invalid: locking and producer cleanup still passed on head and base tip.

leads.summary: The new comment identifies the wrong fallback on Omarchy's default system bus
leads.consequence: Omarchy's default Arch system bus is dbus-broker v37. It expressly rejects eavesdrop=true in AddMatch for unprivileged clients; dbus-monitor retries the match without that key. Likewise dbus-daemon v1.16.2 requires privilege for eavesdrop=true. The fallback that delivers broadcast PrepareForSleep is ordinary, non-eavesdropping AddMatch, not functioning eavesdropping. There is no demonstrated lock regression from this fact, but the PR's explanation of what can be safely silenced and why the signal arrives is inaccurate; adjust the comment to state the non-eavesdropping fallback explicitly.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The bus still logs its own `BecomeMonitor` denial on every start, so the journal is not quiet with this change.

### The bus still logs the denial

The bus also logs the refused `BecomeMonitor` call: dbus-broker (the Arch default) writes `A security policy denied ... BecomeMonitor` at warning level, and dbus-daemon writes `Rejected send message`. The #7316 journal shows the dbus-broker line next to the notice, and the unit restarts after every resume (`Restart=always`), so this repeats per suspend. #10394 (`Fixes #10317`) uses `gdbus monitor`, which never calls `BecomeMonitor`, and conflicts with this PR.

**Suggested change:** Pick one approach with #10394, or link #10317 and note that the bus-side line remains.

<details><summary>Reproducer (dbus-daemon line still present at 78775b5)</summary>

# Bus-side BecomeMonitor denial is still logged with the PR applied

Reviewed head: 78775b5da4cfdbd5175b47d1a49df645293541f9 (base 692c02cad5).

Save as `daemon-log-repro.sh` and run it as a normal user from the root of an Omarchy checkout: `bash daemon-log-repro.sh .`. It needs only the `dbus-daemon` and `dbus-monitor` binaries from the Arch `dbus` package. It starts a private `dbus-daemon` with the shipped `/usr/share/dbus-1/system.conf` policy (minus the daemon user, fork, pidfile, service-dir and include lines), runs the sleep monitor with the real `dbus-monitor` against it, and prints the monitor stderr and the daemon log. Limitation: the private daemon runs as the invoking user, so its AddMatch eavesdrop check passes here; on a real system bus (daemon user `dbus`, or dbus-broker, the Arch default) the eavesdrop rule is refused and dbus-monitor retries with an ordinary match. dbus-broker logs its own line instead: `A security policy denied :1.N to send method call /org/freedesktop/DBus:org.freedesktop.DBus.Monitoring.BecomeMonitor to org.freedesktop.DBus.` (see issue #7316).

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: daemon-log-repro.sh OMARCHY_CHECKOUT
# Runs the sleep monitor with the real dbus-monitor against a private
# dbus-daemon that uses the shipped system bus policy, then prints the
# monitor's stderr and the daemon's own log. Run as a normal user.

set -euo pipefail

root=$1
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
daemon_pid=""
monitor_pid=""
cleanup() {
  [[ -n $monitor_pid ]] && kill "$monitor_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  [[ -n $daemon_pid ]] && kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# The shipped policy, minus the parts that need root or the real system.
sed -e '/<user>/d' -e '/<fork\/>/d' -e '/<pidfile>/d' -e '/<servicehelper>/d' \
  -e '/<standard_system_servicedirs\/>/d' -e '/<includedir>/d' -e '/<include /d' \
  -e "s|<listen>.*</listen>|<listen>unix:path=$tmp/system_bus_socket</listen>|" \
  /usr/share/dbus-1/system.conf >"$tmp/system.conf"

dbus-daemon --config-file="$tmp/system.conf" --nofork --nopidfile --nosyslog \
  --print-address=3 3>"$tmp/address" 2>"$tmp/daemon.log" &
daemon_pid=$!
for _ in {1..200}; do
  [[ -s $tmp/address ]] && break
  sleep 0.01
done
[[ -s $tmp/address ]] || { echo "dbus-daemon did not start" >&2; exit 1; }

mkdir -p "$tmp/bin" "$tmp/omarchy/bin"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nwhile [[ $1 == --* ]]; do shift; done\nexec "$@"\n' >"$tmp/bin/systemd-inhibit"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho locked\n' >"$tmp/omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock"
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/systemd-inhibit" "$tmp/omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock"
ln -s "$root/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor" "$tmp/omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor"

DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS=$(head -n1 "$tmp/address") \
  OMARCHY_PATH="$tmp/omarchy" PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" \
  "$root/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor" 2>"$tmp/monitor.log" &
monitor_pid=$!

for _ in {1..300}; do
  grep -q BecomeMonitor "$tmp/daemon.log" && break
  sleep 0.01
done

kill "$monitor_pid"
wait "$monitor_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
monitor_pid=""
sleep 0.2 # let the stderr filter, which is not a child of the monitor, flush

echo "--- id -u: $(id -u)"
echo "--- sleep monitor stderr"
sed -E 's/pid=[0-9]+/pid=N/' "$tmp/monitor.log"
echo "--- dbus-daemon log"
sed -E 's/pid=[0-9]+/pid=N/; s/dbus-daemon\[[0-9]+\]/dbus-daemon[N]/' "$tmp/daemon.log"
```

Actual output (run inside the review sandbox as uid 1000; pids normalized by the script):

```text
$ bash daemon-log-repro.sh .   # at base
--- id -u: 1000
--- sleep monitor stderr
dbus-monitor: unable to enable new-style monitoring: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied: "Rejected send message, 1 matched rules; type="method_call", sender=":1.0" (uid=1000 pid=N comm="dbus-monitor --system type='signal',sender='org.fr") interface="org.freedesktop.DBus.Monitoring" member="BecomeMonitor" error name="(unset)" requested_reply="0" destination="org.freedesktop.DBus" (bus)". Falling back to eavesdropping.
--- dbus-daemon log
dbus-daemon[N]: [system] Rejected send message, 1 matched rules; type="method_call", sender=":1.0" (uid=1000 pid=N comm="dbus-monitor --system type='signal',sender='org.fr") interface="org.freedesktop.DBus.Monitoring" member="BecomeMonitor" error name="(unset)" requested_reply="0" destination="org.freedesktop.DBus" (bus)
(exit status 0)

$ bash daemon-log-repro.sh .   # at head
--- id -u: 1000
--- sleep monitor stderr
--- dbus-daemon log
dbus-daemon[N]: [system] Rejected send message, 1 matched rules; type="method_call", sender=":1.0" (uid=1000 pid=N comm="dbus-monitor --system type='signal',sender='org.fr") interface="org.freedesktop.DBus.Monitoring" member="BecomeMonitor" error name="(unset)" requested_reply="0" destination="org.freedesktop.DBus" (bus)
(exit status 0)
```

</details>

<details><summary>More findings: other stderr is held until dbus-monitor exits</summary>

`grep` block-buffers its output to the journal. A non-notice line printed while `dbus-monitor` keeps running appears only when it exits, and a SIGTERM to the process group while it ran discarded the line. A stand-in fatal line printed right before exit still arrived in all 35 runs per commit.

**Suggested change:** Use `2> >(grep --line-buffered -v "unable to enable new-style monitoring" >&2)`.
</details>

# Unfiltered dbus-monitor stderr is held until dbus-monitor exits

Reviewed head: 78775b5da4cfdbd5175b47d1a49df645293541f9 (base 692c02cad5).

Save as `test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-stderr-timing-test.sh` in an Omarchy checkout and run `bash test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-stderr-timing-test.sh`. It uses the same stubs as `sleep-monitor-test.sh`. The stand-in dbus-monitor writes the notice plus one other warning to stderr and keeps running. At the reviewed head, `grep` block-buffers its output (stderr is a file here, a journal socket in the unit), so the warning appears only after dbus-monitor exits. Adding `--line-buffered` to the `grep` makes it pass (checked separately in the fixture). Practical impact is low: every other message dbus-monitor itself prints is followed by exit, and those lines arrived in all 35 runs even when the process group got SIGTERM right after the monitor exited.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

sleep_monitor="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor"
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

mock_bin="$tmpdir/bin"
mock_omarchy="$tmpdir/omarchy"
stderr_log="$tmpdir/stderr"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin" "$mock_omarchy/bin"

cat >"$mock_bin/systemd-inhibit" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

while [[ $1 == --* ]]; do
  shift
done

exec "$@"
SH

# A warning written while dbus-monitor keeps running, with no sleep event yet.
cat >"$mock_bin/dbus-monitor" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

echo 'dbus-monitor: unable to enable new-style monitoring: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied: "Sender is not authorized to send message". Falling back to eavesdropping.' >&2
echo 'example warning while running' >&2
exec sleep 30
SH

cat >"$mock_omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
SH

chmod +x \
  "$mock_bin/systemd-inhibit" \
  "$mock_bin/dbus-monitor" \
  "$mock_omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock"
ln -s "$sleep_monitor" "$mock_omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor"

OMARCHY_PATH="$mock_omarchy" PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH" "$sleep_monitor" 2>"$stderr_log" &
monitor_pid=$!

seen_while_running=false
for _ in {1..100}; do
  if grep -q 'example warning while running' "$stderr_log"; then
    seen_while_running=true
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.01
done

stderr_while_running=$(<"$stderr_log")
kill "$monitor_pid"
wait "$monitor_pid" 2>/dev/null || true

[[ $seen_while_running == "true" ]] ||
  fail "dbus-monitor stderr reaches the log while dbus-monitor is still running" "stderr after 1s: '$stderr_while_running'"
pass "dbus-monitor stderr reaches the log while dbus-monitor is still running"
```

Actual output (run inside the review sandbox, from a copy of the checkout with the file added; stdout then stderr):

```text
$ bash test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-stderr-timing-test.sh   # at base
ok - dbus-monitor stderr reaches the log while dbus-monitor is still running
(exit status 0)

$ bash test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-stderr-timing-test.sh   # at head
stderr after 1s: ''
not ok - dbus-monitor stderr reaches the log while dbus-monitor is still running
(exit status 1)
```

</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- Real `dbus-monitor` 1.16.2 on a private `dbus-daemon` (shipped policy plus test-only rules for a stand-in login1): `PrepareForSleep(true)` triggers the lock at base and head; `(false)` does not.
- With a stand-in `dbus-monitor`: exit status is unchanged at base and head (lock path and SIGTERM).
- With a stand-in `dbus-monitor`: the filter drops the notice (and its "dbus-daemon is too old" variant) and keeps other lines, including a `Failed to setup match` line.
- From systemd source: the filter process cannot hold the inhibitor lock, because `systemd-inhibit` closes extra fds in its child.

**Related open PRs:** besides #10394, #7447 conflicts on the adjacent `exec` line (keep both edits), and #13005 restructures the monitor into a shared helper, so the filter would need to be reapplied there.

**Optional notes:**
- The new comment says `dbus-monitor` "falls back to eavesdropping". dbus-broker rejects `eavesdrop=true` in AddMatch outright, and dbus-daemon only allows them for privileged callers; `dbus-monitor` then retries with an ordinary match rule, which is what receives this broadcast. Suggested wording: "...logs a notice and retries with an ordinary match rule, which receives this broadcast signal."
- `test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-test.sh` passes at base, head and with a mutant that drops all `dbus-monitor` stderr, so it does not cover the filter. The test below fails at base and passes at head.

# Suggested regression test for the filter (passes at head, fails at base)

Reviewed head: 78775b5da4cfdbd5175b47d1a49df645293541f9 (base 692c02cad5).

Not a defect reproducer: this is coverage the PR could add. The existing `sleep-monitor-test.sh` passes at the base, at the head and with a mutant that drops all dbus-monitor stderr, so it does not cover this change. Save as `test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-stderr-test.sh` (or fold into `sleep-monitor-test.sh`) and run `bash test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-stderr-test.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

sleep_monitor="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor"
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

mock_bin="$tmpdir/bin"
mock_omarchy="$tmpdir/omarchy"
stderr_log="$tmpdir/stderr"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin" "$mock_omarchy/bin"

cat >"$mock_bin/systemd-inhibit" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

while [[ $1 == --* ]]; do
  shift
done

exec "$@"
SH

cat >"$mock_bin/dbus-monitor" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

echo 'dbus-monitor: unable to enable new-style monitoring: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied: "Sender is not authorized to send message". Falling back to eavesdropping.' >&2
echo 'Failed to setup match "type=signal": example error' >&2
printf '   boolean true\n'
exec sleep 30
SH

cat >"$mock_omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
SH

chmod +x \
  "$mock_bin/systemd-inhibit" \
  "$mock_bin/dbus-monitor" \
  "$mock_omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock"
ln -s "$sleep_monitor" "$mock_omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor"

OMARCHY_PATH="$mock_omarchy" PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH" "$sleep_monitor" 2>"$stderr_log"

# The filter is not a child of the monitor, so give it a moment to flush.
for _ in {1..100}; do
  grep -q 'example error' "$stderr_log" && break
  sleep 0.01
done

if grep -q 'unable to enable new-style monitoring' "$stderr_log"; then
  fail "sleep monitor drops the BecomeMonitor fallback notice" "$(<"$stderr_log")"
fi
pass "sleep monitor drops the BecomeMonitor fallback notice"

grep -q 'example error' "$stderr_log" ||
  fail "sleep monitor keeps other dbus-monitor stderr" "$(<"$stderr_log")"
pass "sleep monitor keeps other dbus-monitor stderr"
```
